body:
# the contributor audit of two actual convex centroid corrections

## Minimum-mass one-cap correction: PASS

Read `candidate d77abe6ff171c6f3` in
full and ran its Fraction verifier, which passed. The removal LP is
feasible using the actual added fiber masses, compact, and dualized with
the correct sign. Its relation r_*=m_E-T_j(E) is exact. The cited proved
moment-realization theorem supplies one actual cap, not the requested
individual fiber removal profile. Its opposite CLOSED cap has exactly
the corrected moments because every full-dimensional fiber assigns the
shared nonvertical boundary measure zero. The positive retained measure
ensures an actual ambient convex body.

The local gauge criterion includes the capacity hypothesis. Every
nonnegative optimal coefficient is at most their total mass, so a total
below every capacity suffices. Its dual and the exposed-face equality
case give the claimed first-order gain characterization in the relative
base span, with rank zero treated separately.

The cap correction need not retain the old source. The proof explicitly
uses the signed measure identity mu_new=mu_old+added-removed, accounts
for actual deleted OLD mass, and bounds the true continuous centroid
shift by R(delta+r)/(m+delta-r). Coarea with a unit CONTINUOUS normal
makes its cap bound uniform over all integer tilts. Vertical closed caps
keep their threshold and boundary fiber. The stated sufficient slack
conditions have all three necessary costs and do not claim to settle
zero slack.

The two rectangle constructions are actual compatible convex-fiber
hulls; the displayed cap removes exactly the strip claimed and no
other fiber. The centered example's continuous centroid, total mass,
and rational gamma2 comparison pass. For the strict-slack face-saturation
corollary, proper convex inclusion gives strict volume increase and
Brunn--Minkowski gives a positive first mixed-volume derivative. Failure
of strict corrected gain then places EVERY growing base in one proper
exposed face. This reasoning is correctly restricted to strict slack.

## Exponential inner erosion: root proof check

Read `candidate 1357de39d4196ea9`
in full. A convex nonnegative radius over the real base gives an actual
convex fiberwise erosion by the displayed Minkowski inclusion, including
all intermediate noninteger bases. The small-loss argument uses the
inner distance coarea formula and continuous convex surface area, with
a common positive fiber inradius. These give the stated uniform C1
limit on every bounded parameter set. The exponential moment Hessian
is positive definite on the relative base span, and the explicit
contraction argument yields finite exact parameters, not merely formal
derivative equations. No boundary loss-mean conclusion is asserted.

The polyhedral unused-point bulge has linear positive growth in its own
fiber and total growth O(t). In the relaxed-polytope upper bound, purely
vertical inequalities may be ignored at a fixed base; the remaining
continuous inequalities have a strict interior fiber witness, giving
the claimed uniform homothetic bound. The positive fraction of added
mass at an interior base places the added mean in a compact interior
subset. The prior local argument then applies uniformly.

The exact cap payment identity retains the signed added/removed first
moment and the new true centroid. Its influence function is asserted
only when the limiting surface/addition laws give the plane no mass;
the all-cap example instead checks the coincident clipping boundaries
directly. Its four extremal mass expressions follow from the complete
six-breakpoint slope order and cover BOTH nonvertical orientations.
Vertical caps dominate the limiting values. No sign condition for an
arbitrary maximal extractor is claimed.

The Sympy exact verifier passes under the workspace mathematical Python
environment. The independent functional audit of this erosion note is
being carried out separately; any resulting edits remain to be incorporated.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
